problems.title: 60-Hour Weekend Gap — Leads Die While the Clinic Is Closed
problems.description: People decide to pursue bariatric surgery late at night and on weekends — moments of peak emotional motivation after seeing themselves in a photo, hitting a health scare, or failing another diet. SFSBI is closed Friday at 12:30 PM until Monday at 9 AM — a 60+ hour blackout window. Web forms sit unanswered. Calls go to voicemail. The competitor who responds at 10 PM Sunday owns that patient.
problems.impact: Practices responding within 5 minutes are 21x more likely to convert than those waiting 30 minutes. At $20K avg surgery revenue, every 3 missed leads = $60K lost.
problems.evidence: SFSBI hours: Mon–Thu 9–4:30, Fri 9–12:30, closed all weekend. Online scheduling exists but no AI response layer captures or engages inquiries outside business hours.

problems.title: 3–6 Month Pre-Op Journey Has No System — Patients Ghost
problems.description: Insurance requires 6 months of supervised diet documentation, psych clearance, nutritional counseling, and multiple medical clearances. That's 6 months of friction where patients can quit, pivot to GLP-1s, or simply lose momentum. Without proactive nurture at every stage, 40–60% of consultations never reach surgery. Each lost patient mid-pipeline is $15,000–$35,000 of revenue that disappears after they've already met the surgeon.
problems.impact: Losing 1 patient per week mid-pipeline at $20K avg = $80K/month in pipeline leakage. Even a 20% recovery = $16K/month recaptured.
problems.evidence: Bariatric surgery industry average: ~40–60% of consulted patients never reach the operating table without active journey management.

problems.title: Insurance Navigation Nightmare — Patients Abandon at the Paperwork Wall
problems.description: Pre-authorization for bariatric surgery is brutal: BMI criteria documentation, 6-month supervised diet records, psychological evaluation, multiple physician letters of medical necessity, and a 4–8 week wait for approval. Patients who don't understand what's required — or who hit a denial — abandon the process entirely. Staff spend hours on insurance phone calls and appeals instead of clinical work.
problems.impact: Each insurance abandonment = $20K surgery lost. Pre-auth errors add 2–4 weeks per denial round. Documentation errors cost $0 to fix but derail the entire timeline.
problems.evidence: Pre-authorization alone takes 2–4 weeks. Re-submissions after denials add another 2–4 weeks. 15% denial rate means ~3 patients/month hitting the paperwork wall.

problems.title: Post-Op Follow-Up Collapse — 93.5% of Patients Gone by Year 2
problems.description: By 24 months post-op, only 6.5% of bariatric patients are still attending follow-up appointments. By 12 months it's already 29.6%. This isn't just a clinical failure — it's a revenue failure. Lapsed patients miss critical lab work (B12, iron, protein), don't get body contouring consultations, and represent a massive dormant revenue opportunity. SFSBI has both bariatric AND cosmetic capabilities — making this gap even more costly.
problems.impact: 50 reactivated post-op patients/year at $500/visit = $25K recovered. Body contouring upsell to 20% of surgical patients at $10K avg = $50K+ additional annual revenue.
problems.evidence: PubMed: Postoperative Follow-up Compliance: The Achilles' Heel of Bariatric Surgery. 12-month compliance: 29.6%. 24-month: 6.5%.

problems.title: GLP-1 Objection Handling — Every Prospect Is Now Comparing Surgery vs. Ozempic
problems.description: Bariatric surgery volume dropped 46.4% from Q4 2022 to Q3 2025 because of GLP-1 drugs. Every prospect SFSBI speaks to is now evaluating surgery vs. Ozempic/Wegovy. Staff have no consistent messaging. Prospects who leave 'to try Ozempic first' almost never come back — until they fail. Surgery produces 5x more weight loss than GLP-1s (58 lbs vs 12 lbs at 2 years). The clinic that educates before the consult wins the patient.
problems.impact: Every prospect lost to GLP-1s represents $20K in delayed or lost revenue. Capturing GLP-1 failures is the fastest-growing bariatric segment right now.
problems.evidence: Surgery vs GLP-1s — Johns Hopkins Medicine. Bariatric surgery volumes continue falling amid GLP-1 boom — Becker's. STAT News: bariatric surgery volume down 46.4%.

problems.title: 22% Consultation No-Show Rate — $20K+ Surgeries Never Start
problems.description: Specialty clinic no-show rates run 18–30%. A missed free consultation is not just an empty slot — it's a $15,000–$35,000 surgery that never gets started. With 20 monthly consultations and a 22% no-show rate, that's 4–5 surgeries per month that never begin. A multi-touch reminder sequence and waitlist system would recover most of these.
problems.impact: 4–5 missed consultations/month × $20K avg surgery = $80K–$100K/month in pipeline revenue that never starts.
problems.evidence: Specialty clinic no-show rate benchmark: 18–30%. DialogHealth patient no-show statistics. Each free consultation is the entry point to a $15K–$35K procedure.

problems.title: Thin Review Profile in a High-Stakes Decision Market
problems.description: Choosing bariatric surgery is one of the most consequential health decisions a person makes. Patients obsessively research reviews before ever calling. Miami has major hospital bariatric programs and established clinics with hundreds of reviews. SFSBI's boutique positioning is a strength — but a thin Google review footprint undermines trust before the first call. A patient posting 'Dr. Valladares changed my life — I'm down 95 lbs' is worth 10 routine reviews in this space.
problems.impact: Thin review profile = prospects choosing hospital systems or larger clinics. In Miami's competitive cosmetic/bariatric market, trust signals drive the first call.
problems.evidence: High-stakes healthcare decisions: patients average 5–7 sources of research before first call. Miami market: competing against major hospital bariatric programs.

problems.title: The Body Contouring Upsell Is Being Left on the Table
problems.description: Massive weight loss (80–150 lbs) leaves excess skin. Virtually every surgical patient becomes a candidate for body contouring — panniculectomy, brachioplasty, thigh lift, tummy tuck. SFSBI performs cosmetic surgery. But without a system to introduce this at the right time (12–18 months post-op when weight stabilizes), they're leaving $8K–$15K+ per patient untouched. If only 20% of surgical patients convert to body contouring at $10K avg — that's significant recurring revenue from patients they already have.
problems.impact: 25 surgeries/year × 20% body contouring conversion × $10K avg = $50K additional annual revenue from existing patients.
problems.evidence: SFSBI offers full cosmetic surgery including body contouring. Standard bariatric timeline: weight stabilizes at 12–18 months, creating the ideal body contouring window.
